requirements.evidence: All contract pieces present: migrations with cascading FKs, unique (queue_id, code) and the recommended index (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_tickets_table.php:14-28); Queue model with Fillable/casts/relations (app/Models/Queue.php:11-44); Entity::queues() (app/Models/Entity.php:46); enums; InactiveQueueException extends RuntimeException; IssueTicket locks the queue row inside the transaction and re-checks is_active (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:53-60), rejects negative priority (:44), retries on unique collisions (:48-75); write-once updating hook (app/Models/Ticket.php:84-94); call() locks, checks status and membership (app/Models/Ticket.php:167-198); factories with forQueue and code allocation. Deviations at the edges: nextCode uses max(highWater, lastValid) (Ticket.php:146), so an explicit out-of-order valid code (e.g. A999 then A005) yields A1000 rather than the specified 'last valid code in insertion order + 1'; in call() the status check runs before the membership check (Ticket.php:179-190), so a non-member calling an already-called ticket gets LogicException instead of AuthorizationException.

conventions.evidence: Domain write goes through App\Actions\IssueTicket; $fillable set via #[Fillable]; migrations have down(); business-rules.md, database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md updated in the same change. Deviations: the entity-membership authorization in Ticket::call is a hand-written EntityMembership query (Ticket.php:183-190), not a policy or gate; the migration timestamps 2026_10_29_000000/000001 look hand-named rather than generated by make:migration; IssueTicket.php:78 uses an inline '\LogicException' while sibling code imports its exceptions.

security.evidence: No HTTP/Livewire surface. call() authorizes server-side against entity membership inside a locked transaction and leaves the ticket unchanged on failure (tested at tests/Feature/Queue/TicketDomainTest.php:913-926). Issuance re-reads and locks the queue rather than trusting the passed model. Small gaps: authorization is ad hoc and not in a reusable policy, and the order of checks in call() lets a non-member learn a ticket's status (LogicException versus AuthorizationException). Ticket $fillable includes status/called_by_user_id, which is acceptable for now but loose.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/Queue/TicketDomainTest.php covers the schema and indexes, relations and casts, code sequencing including A-X, A999->A1000->A1001 and deletion (lines 788-818), factory allocation and explicit codes, IssueTicket defaults/priority/channel, negative priority, inactive and stale-deactivated queues with nothing persisted (879-898), call by a member, a non-member, a double call, write-once on code and priority, and cascade delete. Not covered: the unique-collision retry path in IssueTicket, the TicketFactory::create count override (e.g. ->count(2)->create()), and a non-member calling an already-called ticket.

simplicity.evidence: Code allocation uses two overlapping mechanisms: a queues.last_ticket_number high-water mark that is advanced in created, in deleting and inside nextCode itself (Ticket.php:76-82, 143-152), plus a full pluck of every code in the queue on each issuance (Ticket.php:139-142). The read-sounding nextCode() writes to the database. IssueTicket::isUniqueConstraintViolation (IssueTicket.php:81-94) parses SQLSTATE codes and message strings by hand even though Laravel provides UniqueConstraintViolationException, and its check for '23000' also matches other integrity violations. TicketFactory overrides create() (TicketFactory.php:510-517) to work around nextCode being called at make time.

readability.evidence: Names are clear, comments explain the reasoning (IssueTicket.php:51-52, Ticket.php:327-328), and the methods are short. Minor issues: the private advanceCodeHighWater sits between the public relation methods; nextCode's docblock does not mention that it mutates queues.last_ticket_number; IssueTicket.php:78 is an effectively unreachable throw.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: domain classes, migrations, factories, one test file, and the docs/CHANGELOG updates the task asked for. The extra last_ticket_number column supports the no-reuse rule and is documented. No HTTP, Livewire or call-next selection was added.

issues.explanation: max(highWater, lastValid) means the next code is not 'last valid code in insertion order + 1' when a lower explicit code is inserted after a higher one (A999 then A005 yields A1000, not A006).
The status check runs before the membership check, so a non-member calling an already-called ticket gets LogicException rather than AuthorizationException and learns the ticket's state.
Membership authorization is an inline EntityMembership query instead of a policy/gate, contrary to 'Authorization always goes through policies/gates'.
nextCode plucks every code of the queue on each issuance and also writes the high-water mark, duplicating the created/deleting hooks; the counter and the code scan overlap.

Hand-rolled unique-violation detection based on SQLSTATE and message strings, where catching Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException would do; '23000' also matches non-unique integrity errors.
The collision retry path and the TicketFactory::create count override are untested.
The 000000/000001 timestamps suggest hand-named migrations rather than ones generated with make:migration.
Effectively unreachable throw using a fully qualified \LogicException instead of an import, unlike the rest of the file.

review.summary: The change adds queues/tickets migrations, models, enums, factories, the IssueTicket action with a locked re-check of the queue and a collision retry, write-once and single-call rules, docs and a thorough Pest suite. It meets the task and conventions well. The deductions are for an overlapping code-allocation design (high-water mark plus a full code scan with side effects), hand-rolled unique-violation detection and ad hoc authorization ordering. These are worth fixing but do not block merging.
